[RLOW.6.1.9] **A rounding of a dimensioned value lowers through its own unit.** A
value carries no unit at run time: the compiler resolves the value's own unit
([LUNI.8.9]) from its static type. Where the dimension's storage is `float64`
([LUNI.7.2]), the compiler must lower `round(x)`, `math.floor(x)`, `math.ceil(x)`
and `math.trunc(x)` to the conversion of `x` from the base unit that
[RLOW.7.3.9] builds, then the builtin, then `FN_INT_TO_FLOAT`, then the unit's
conversion to the base unit, from the arithmetic expression nodes the engine
already evaluates. A `Float` with no `Int` answer raises as [LEXP.3.2] states.

Where the storage is an integer, `int64` or `int32` ([LUNI.4.1.1]), and the unit
is tier-1, the compiler must lower each of the four in `Int` arithmetic, with no
`Float` operand, so that no value loses precision. With $P$, $Q$ and $R$ as
[RLOW.6.1.10] states them, the value in the unit is the exact quotient
$(Q x - R) / P$, for either sign of $P$ ([LUNI.4.3]). The builtin gives its
integer $n$, ties to even for `round`, and the result is $n$ taken back to the
base unit as [RLOW.6.1.10] lowers `n::<unit>`, raising as that lowering does
when $n$ units are not a whole number of base units. Where the unit is tier-2, the
four lower as on `float64` storage, with `x` converted round-to-nearest-even
and the result cast as [LUNI.7.2] states.

Where the storage is `float64`, the compiler must lower `math.sign(x)` to the
same conversion from the base unit, then the builtin. Where it is an integer and
the unit is tier-1, the compiler must lower `math.sign(x)` to the builtin over
`Q·x - R`, negated when $P$ is negative: the sign of $(Q x - R) / P$, with no
division. Where it is an integer and the unit is tier-2, `math.sign(x)` lowers as
on `float64` storage. The compiler's constant folder
must fold each of the five to the value its lowering computes ([LDET.3.3a.8]).
